title: Request Replay Chronicle: compact timeline + span-context pane
creator: Lena Novak
description: Goal: Design a compact, scannable 'Request Replay Chronicle' that helps engineers replay and understand a single request end-to-end. This view combines a horizontally scrollable span timeline with a correlated metadata ribbon (correlation IDs, route, model variant) and a contextual right-hand pane for span-level details, logs, and related errors. The emphasis is on: 1) fast triage (find slow spans and errors in 3 clicks), 2) correlating spans to logs/metrics, and 3) low-noise presentation for long trace trees (collapse/aggregation heuristics). This ticket covers low-fidelity -> high-fidelity prototypes, pattern decisions, accessibility checks, and a handoff spec for implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype includes timeline with span nesting and duration bars, with hover preview of span metadata
Correlation ribbon present above timeline: request id, trace id, user id, route, model variant (each linkable to filters)
Filter panel supports quick toggles: show errors only, durations > X ms, service name, tag key/value
Mini-map overview with scrubber to quickly jump to long traces
Right-hand detail pane shows span payload, linked logs (timestamped), and a breadcrumb of parent spans
Collapsed spans algorithm: long sequences auto-aggregate with count + total time and expand affordance
Responsiveness: layout adapts to small consoles; timeline becomes vertical stacked on narrow widths
A11y: keyboard navigation between spans and focusable scrubber; color contrast meets WCAG AA
Design spec includes tokenized CSS vars, spacing, and margin guidelines for engineering handoff
Figma prototype link and at least one usability snapshot attached
design_decisions: Show timeline as primary surface rather than flamegraph for quick duration-first triage: engineers told us they scan bars faster than arcs
Aggregation heuristic: collapse sibling spans that are < 5% of parent duration and when there are > 6 siblings, show aggregated pill
Correlation ribbon chosen to live above timeline so filters can be applied at request-level without scrolling
Logs are shown inline in the detail pane rather than overlay to preserve timeline context and avoid modal churn
Prefer explicit link-out icons for external artifacts (GitHub PR, incident runbook) rather than auto-navigating on click to avoid accidental context switches
Accessibility: large interactive hit targets for span bars (min 44px height) and explicit keyboard shortcuts for next/prev span

notes_for_engineering: Include telemetry hooks: span.click, span.expand, scrubber.seek, filter.apply, correlation.copy. Prefer SVG horizontal bars with element-level data attributes for safe mutation. Provide guidance for virtualized rendering and lazy-loading linked logs.
open_questions: Should aggregated span pills surface the top 1-2 representative child spans in a tooltip or a compact inline list?
How should we handle multi-model requests where the same request spawns parallel model calls - show parallel lanes or stack them?
Do we expose sampling indicator (sample rate) on request meta ribbon?
